messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Survival rate out of apparent survival in openCR spatial
parts:
Hi Stefano
What is this "a"? If you successfully model between-session movement in openCR.fit then the reported estimates of phi are estimates of actual survival. That is a big 'if': it depends on a good match between the study design and dispersal biology of your species, and on correct use of somewhat tricky software. You should at least use the latest version of openCR (1.4.1) that was only submitted yesterday to CRAN and is not yet fully distributed (but see section on movement kernels in  https://www.otago.ac.nz/density/pdfs/openCR-vignette.pdf).
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Survival rate out of apparent survival in openCR spatial
parts:
I really don't know. I have doubts about whether local capture-recapture data can be modelled adequately to adjust for losses due to long-distance dispersal. On the other hand, we have submitted some work that suggests robustness to misspecification of the dispersal model. I cannot say how this applies in your case, and I doubt there are general answers. The way forward is probably to confirm model behaviour by simulating your particular scenario, which I know would be a burden. Richard Glennie's software openpopscr on GiTHub is an alternative that does not require truncation of the kernel at a pre-determined radius, but that may fail to deal with long-distance dispersal (fat tails) because it is limited to bivariate normal kernels.
Murray
